propositions: The test kills its pytest-xdist worker intermittently on macOS py3.13 because a single monolithic test loop processing 884 renderable units with ~1768 serial pandoc spawns exceeds the 300s per-test timeout guard when CPU-saturated (measured 504.8s vs 91.6s idle)

The timeout-method=thread setting causes os._exit(1) from a timer thread, terminating the worker process without a traceback or assertion text, so the failure appears as a worker crash rather than a test failure

The test's cost is unbounded and load-dependent: corpus-wide comparison is pinned to a single test function, preventing xdist from distributing work across workers and amplifying macOS runner pool contention

Chunking the equivalence comparison into fixed-size batches (40-unit chunks per _EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK) bounds per-test cost structurally: corpus growth adds test cases rather than extending any single case's duration
All 884 units must remain compared against the oracle with real pandoc and stride-1 sampling to preserve the byte-identity property the test protects
A coverage guard test (test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit) must verify that all chunks reassemble to exactly _renderable_units() and total >= 100 to prevent silent unit drops
